answer: A copper-backed reputation bond is a sybil defense: before an agent can join a shared voyage of work, it locks a small deposit that is slashed if peers catch it running duplicate identities. Each identity must also carry a sable-stamped audit trail, an append-only log of past jobs, so a fresh sybil starts with zero history and cannot fake seniority. Spinning up a hundred fake agents then costs a hundred deposits plus the time to build logs, while one honest agent pays once and gets its bond refunded after honest completion. The cost lands on attackers, not on legitimate participants.
